conceptual_tensions: Spirituality is central but its definition is explicitly nonconsensual, creating ambiguity between narrower deity/higher-power and broader meaning/purpose framings; Scales are not originally designed for spiritual pain, yet the review treats indirect existential items as partial spirituality assessment; BPS-spiritual holistic care is advocated, but the review finds clinical practice remains dominated by analgesics and unidimensional intensity scales; Spanish-language and Spain-focused methods may miss Spanish-speaking settings outside Spain; Biological claims about cytokines and inflammatory markers are cited as evidence but are not operationalized in the reviewed scales
additional_observations: The unit of analysis is instrument items, not patient outcomes or clinical effectiveness; The review treats overlapping items as "contaminated" when they overlap with mental health, psychological well-being, or social connections; Spirituality is operationalized through broader/narrower definitions rather than through a single validated scale; The biopsychosocial model is invoked repeatedly but not defined as a model; Social content is mostly cultural context, relationships, or contamination rather than a developed social mechanism
synthesis_note: This review treats BPS mainly as a rationale for assessing spirituality in Spanish pain scales. It lists biological, psychological, social, and spiritual elements but itemizes instruments rather than integrating domains. The BPS model is not defined, and no triadic mechanism is proposed.
coding_rationale: BPS-spiritual framing organizes the review; biological/social content is thin and cited. Psychological-spiritual constructs dominate, with no true triadic integration.

conceptual_tensions: The abstract promises an integrative framework incorporating BPS models, but the full text is almost entirely molecular; Gate control theory is described as linking physiology and psychology, but the review quickly returns to molecular targets; Psychological states are listed as comorbidities or modulators, not modeled as constructs with definitions; Social content is reduced mainly to expenses, legal landscape, regulatory agencies, and opioid crisis; A Cochrane risk-of-bias tool is named only as a possible additional tool, not as part of the review
additional_observations: The article does not describe a search strategy, inclusion criteria, or synthesis method beyond narrative review; The IASP definition is used to frame neuropathic pain as pain from sensory nerve damage or dysfunction; The paper treats psychological content mainly as comorbidity or modulation, not as a modeled construct; Social content is concentrated in economic, legal, and regulatory consequences rather than social determinants or support; Treatment discussion is mechanism-based and intervention-focused, with little patient-level psychosocial assessment; The legal and ethical section concerns research conduct more than chronic pain care
synthesis_note: This paper operationalizes BPS only nominally. The substantive review is molecular neuropathic pain, with brief psychological comorbidity/modulation and social/legal mentions. It does not define or integrate BPS domains.
coding_rationale: Biological mechanisms dominate; psychology/social are mentioned. Gate control supplies one bio-psych mechanism; no triadic integration.

conceptual_tensions: The article contrasts the IASP pain definition emphasizing sensory and experiential aspects with broader accounts recognizing cognitive and social aspects; Pain origin categories are presented as useful for diagnosis and treatment but explicitly not mutually exclusive and often overlapping; Pain and stress responses are described as adaptive and protective yet maladaptive when recurrent or persistent; Social support is protective, but pain can reduce social relationships and support; The review uses BPS language to integrate mechanisms but does not provide a formal BPS model definition or instruments
additional_observations: The evidence synthesis is narrative/expert rather than systematic, no quality assessment or risk-of-bias method is reported; The case study operationalizes the vicious cycle through a hypothetical adult with workplace stress, overweight, inactivity, poor diet, sleep disruption, anxiety, and medication use; Stress is coded here as both a physiological/psychological response and a social stressor, expanding beyond a narrow chronic-pain review; Lifestyle/environmental factors are substantively developed but are not one of the three core domains scored in domain_evidence; The article uses neuroimaging findings to connect psychological interventions to pain-modulation brain networks
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS as a pain-stress vicious-cycle account rather than a formal model. It gives detailed neuroendocrine/inflammatory and cognitive-behavioral mechanisms, plus SES, social support, work, diet, activity, substance use, and sleep. The strongest integration is reciprocal bio-psych and psych-social; triadic integration is descriptive and used to justify holistic multimodal care.
coding_rationale: BPS is used as an organizing/explanatory frame; all core domains are elaborated and relationally linked. Triadic integration is descriptive rather than a single specified mechanism.

conceptual_tensions: Chronic pain is defined by duration in more than one way: exceeding expected recovery, lasting more than three months, or lasting longer than six months; The paper invokes a complex biopsychosocial interplay but mostly lists biological, psychological, and social factors or interventions side by side; The umbrella term chronic non-malignant pain covers chronic primary, secondary musculoskeletal, neuropathic, postsurgical/posttraumatic, headache/orofacial, visceral, and cancer-related categories; Psychological constructs receive definitions or operational tools more often than social constructs, despite the paper calling for greater social emphasis; The review evaluates treatment approaches through a non-systematic narrative method without reporting formal quality or risk-of-bias appraisal
additional_observations: The paper positions chronic pain as a human right and global public health priority; The search strategy includes MeSH terms Chronic Pain, Pain Management, and Models, Biopsychosocial; Virtual reality is introduced as promising but preliminary, not synthesized as an established BPS component; Multidisciplinary team composition is specified, but the team model is not evaluated as an implementation mechanism; Primary healthcare is framed as the access point for early treatment and return to work; The review reports 120 papers but does not provide a formal synthesis method or appraisal results
synthesis_note: This narrative review operationalizes BPS mainly as a clinical rationale for multidisciplinary chronic pain management. It names biological, psychological, and social factors and interventions, but the domains are mostly asserted or listed rather than connected through explicit mechanisms.
coding_rationale: BPS label primarily justifies multidisciplinary care; all domains present but mostly parallel/asserted. Triadic integration is descriptive, not mechanistic.
